16. Mr. Kamal-ul Alam, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the leave-petitioner, submits that the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the arbitration application is not maintain-able and the same was beyond the jurisdiction of the Court as the applications do not fall within the ambit of "international commercial arbitration'. Such finding is patently wrong, beca6se, under the Arbitration Act,2001, the character of an arbitration, i.e. whether the arbitration is 'domestic or international', is to be determined by referring to the parties to the arbitration agreement not by referring to the parties to the arbitration tribunal and since in the present case there is no dispute that one of the parties to the arbitration agreement was a joint venture which had a partner incorporated in China, the judgment of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. Mr. Alam next submits that the finding of the High Court Division that the time limit of sixty days shall be counted from the date when the applications have been posted in the daily cause list for admission hearing is erroneous, because posting of a case in the daily cause list for a specific purpose is completely at the desire and within the control of the Court and the petitioner can at best submit a case in the concerned Bench or section through its lawyer and as such the aforesaid finding of the High Court Division being not supported by law is liable to be set aside. Mr. Alam emphatically submits that since the matter involves complicated question of law and interpretation of the Arbitration Act, 2001 and the Limitation Act, he prays for granting leave to appeal. 

 20. On the question of .limitation, the High Court Division found that the arbitration applications were admitted after the expiry of 60 days period although affidavit has been sworn in within 60 days. Thus it held that 'the time limit of 60 days shall be counted from the date when the applications have been posted in the daily cause list for admission hearing, not from the date of swearing affidavit and as such the same are barred as well'.
